subject: Post-demo recap: compliance checklist & Trust Vault access for MedGenix POC

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: compliance checklist & Trust Vault access for MedGenix POC

Hi Emily / MedGenix security team,

Thanks for your time today — great conversation and helpful context on your PHI scope and environment. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep the POC moving: 

- Confirm scope: MedGenix will evaluate Redwood for the patient-matching microservice (ingests PII/PHI). You confirmed HIPAA applies; GDPR applies only to EU-subject records (none expected in POC).
- Requested artifacts from our side: SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted), a short bridge letter attesting to current control posture for the POC window, and access to the Redwood Trust Vault (trust portal) so MedGenix security can review evidence.
- Your asks: Completed vendor security questionnaire (VSQ), architecture diagram, and an expected timeline for evidence exchange.

Action items (proposed timeline):
1) MedGenix: upload VSQ to Trust Vault or reply with the spreadsheet by EOD Fri (Oct 2).
2) Redwood: provide SOC 2 Type II redacted summary and bridge letter draft within 2 business days of receiving VSQ.
3) Both: provision Trust Vault access for MedGenix security (invite to security@medgenix.com).

I attached a short SOC2-ask template that outlines what we typically provide for POCs. If you prefer, Aditya (cc'd) can jump into technical details on required evidence and redaction level.

Thanks — looking forward to keeping momentum.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: compliance checklist & Trust Vault access for MedGenix POC

Emily — quick technical clarification and what we can provide: 

- Data flow: for the POC the microservice will receive and emit minimal PHI (patient id/hash plus matching score). Data is encrypted in transit (TLS1.3) and at rest (AES-256). KV caches are ephemeral per-request and not persisted beyond the POC retention window.
- Evidence: we can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II technical summary (control families and testing period), architecture diagram, and a one-page bridge letter that limits claims to POC operations and expected retention/processing.
- Redaction: we usually remove customer names and IPs from the public report; for a deeper review we can provide a controlled-copy under NDA in the Trust Vault.

If you provision Trust Vault access, please invite security@medgenix.com and emily.park@medgenix.com. Once we see the VSQ there are a few control samples we’ll prepare (user access screenshots, key rotation notes) — estimate 2 business days after VSQ receipt. I’ve attached our SOC2_TypeII_Technical_Summary.pdf (redacted summary) for your review.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Principal SE, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
